title: Product comparison after a product-preserving retraction
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be categories [def-nagata-category], $S$ a set small in a fixed universe, and suppose both categories admit products indexed by $S$ [def-weil-category-product]. Let $L:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $J:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be functors. Suppose $J$ preserves these products [def-galois-exact-functor], and let $\theta:JL\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$ be a specified natural isomorphism, meaning $\theta_{A'}\circ JL(f)=f\circ\theta_A$ for every $f:A\to A'$. For any family $(F_s)_{s\in S}$ put $Q=\prod_sF_s$, $P=\prod_sLF_s$, and let $c:LQ\to P$ be the unique map with $\mathrm{pr}_s\circ c=L(\mathrm{pr}_s)$. Let $\beta:JP\to Q$ be the unique map with $\mathrm{pr}_s\circ\beta=\theta_{F_s}\circ J(\mathrm{pr}_s)$. Then $\beta$ is an isomorphism and
$$\beta\circ J(c)=\theta_Q.$$
Consequently $J(c)$ is an isomorphism. The assertion includes $S=\varnothing$.
